title: A large rent-to-own refund reaches a prior-cashing subgroup without proving price correction or durable household relief
source_unit: FTC Progressive Leasing enforcement and repeat-refund program
geography: United States consumers using Progressive Leasing rent-to-own plans

denominator.unit: people reported as receiving a second-round check after cashing the first check and paying Progressive Leasing $616.62 or more

second_round_total.unit: more than U.S. dollars in second-round checks

first_round_total.unit: more than U.S. dollars in first-round refunds sent in June 2021

recipient_condition.value: cashed the first check and paid Progressive Leasing $616.62 or more
recipient_condition.unit: administrative eligibility condition for the second round

underlying_exposure.value: FTC reported that Progressive Leasing misled shoppers about no-interest or same-as-cash pricing and that consumers could pay more than the sticker price, often about twice the sticker price after scheduled payments

second_check_receipt_and_recovery.unit: missing second-check delivery, cashing, contract correction, residual cost, adequacy, household adaptation, and durable exit

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official FTC refund page; alleged pricing exposure, first-round refunds, prior cashing, second-round dispatch, and durable household recovery remain separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The public page does not provide the complete harmed denominator, individual amounts, second-check cashing, contract or debt correction, remaining loss, household substitution, trust, repeat use, switching, or exit. The recipient-conditioned count is not a recovery rate for all affected consumers.
observations.subgroup: Consumers who paid Progressive Leasing at least $616.62 and cashed the first refund check; no income, age, product, retailer, or debt-burden subgroup outcome is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Prior cashing makes the second-round population more reachable, but the condition excludes people who never received or could not cash the first payment; a refund also does not establish that rent-to-own pricing practices or household financial pressure changed.

related_sources.claim: The FTC case page identifies the Progressive Leasing enforcement matter and settlement context.
The FTC describes prior payment cashing, address updates, reissue, and additional-payment stages.

boundary: This record establishes a high-volume rent-to-own pricing enforcement route and a recipient-conditioned second refund. It does not establish second-payment receipt, cashing, contract correction, adequate household recovery, trust, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the official FTC refund-page HTML retrieved through the search.ftc.gov mirror for extraction.
